doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Being a woman in jazz: music has no gender
summary: She cannot know whether she is hired for quotas or music, and says music has no gender, color or flag.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Historically, in the history of jazz it’s been a male dominated business, getting better. I wonder if you feel like you’ve been at a disadvantage or an advantage as being a woman jazz musician or if it just doesn’t matter anymore?

I don’t know the answer. And I can’t tell. Especially this day and age with the Me Too movement. I don’t think I will know if people hire me to play in a festival because I fill in the quota of they have to have women or because they like the music I play. And I will never know what was the reason before. But when people close their eyes and they don’t know who’s playing, the music has no gender and no color and no flag. Music is just music. So I don’t have an answer for that.
Well you’re very quotable I must say that.
